input.quote: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.
input.rationale: Section 20(d) is a flat mutual bar on assignment without the other party's written consent, with no successor/M&A carve-out and no reasonableness standard on consent; Section 3(c) separately prohibits Sparkling from assigning the Agreement except as Garman authorizes in writing. That is walk-away territory (blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out) and fails every fallback element. There is no change-of-control clause anywhere in the document, so Garman has no termination or re-pricing right on our change of control. We target the fallback: mutual successor assignment on written notice, with consent for other assignments not to be unreasonably withheld, and we conform Section 3(c) so it no longer contradicts the new right.

mappings.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
A successor assignment requires written notice.
Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.

proposal.summary: Mutual successor assignment on written notice; other assignments need consent not unreasonably withheld
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a blanket bar on assignment with no successor carve-out, so we have made assignment to a successor to a party's business permissible on written notice, with consent for any other assignment not to be unreasonably withheld. We have also removed the overlapping assignment prohibition in Section 3(c) so the two clauses do not conflict.

ops.oldText: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.
ops.newText: (d) Either party may assign this Agreement to a successor to its business upon written notice to the other party; any other assignment requires the other party's written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
